top_choice_rationale: P002 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) rests on a distinct idea, the magic wavelength that cancels the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, which is not a refinement of the 2005 comb or the 2012 ion-control prizes. The 10^-18 floor has been verified by identifying each systematic shift and by cross-comparisons among laboratories on several continents, and the consequences (gravitational redshift over millimetres, limits on varying constants and dark-matter couplings) are fundamental. The allocation to two names is compact, though it draws a contestable line around Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Hinkley, Takamoto and Bloom. P001 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a genuine and reproduced discovery of new quantum matter and ranks clearly above no award, but it is under a decade old, the pairing mechanism is unsettled, the experimental credit omits Yuan Cao, and I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on priority. A prize is warranted, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund and ETH attosecond groups does not touch Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, though I judge the clock case as an atomic-physics insider
